rationale: The primitive docstring still does not explicitly define whether pi0 is at time zero or at target_t, so the stronger statement that every positive-target single call is wrong is not established. However, the canonical local MODULE.md:42-45 defines all retrodictions as conditionals of one joint process rho on the shared history, and audit_system/CLI accept multiple targets while passing the same unrestricted prior vector to every target. An independent exact-source fixture with T=[[0.8,0.2],[0.1,0.9]], pi0=[1,0], observation S2=B and targets [0,1] returns q0=q1=[1,0]. For any one Markov joint process with this T and observation, the function's own q0 fixes q1 through the Bayesian bridge identity: q1(j)=sum_i q0(i)*T(i,j)*T(j,B)/(T^2)(i,B). Exact rational evaluation requires q1=[8/17,9/17], contradicting the returned [1,0]. This confirms a multi-target temporal-prior coherence defect without assuming pi0's time origin. A stationary-prior control [1/3,2/3] satisfies the identity, showing the scope rather than claiming universal failure. Single-target callers supplying the target marginal can be correct; the public batch must either define a common initial time and propagate its prior, accept target-indexed marginals, or explicitly restrict/check stationary priors. No product or protected runtime was executed, and no remediation was performed.

The canonical contract defines one joint process rho on the history and prediction/retrodiction as its Bayesian conditional marginals. This requires coherence across targets rather than unrelated target-specific processes.
The canonical hub copy has the same SHA-256 as the assigned alias source and the same shared-pi0 batch consumer.

rationale: The command-order observation is correct, but the original allegation treats --dry-run as a nonmutating preview. The explicit local contract says it omits git push, and the successful dry-run output advertises the newly prepared local release branch. Local orphan-commit creation and replacement of this fixed preparation branch therefore do not violate the inspected mode contract. Targeted search across scripts, tests, engine, tools, project skills and guidance found no caller or documented guarantee that this generated branch retains its prior tip. The original candidate does not identify concurrent publication or a mismatch between the attested tree and pushed commit. A separately recorded mutable-ref publication race must not be used to validate this different allegation. Rejection is limited to C0414 as submitted; it does not certify the whole projection script.

rationale: The retained broadcast behavior was correctly observed, but no successive-message requirement or affected reusable consumer was established. After the operator answered that the intended contract was unknown, the root agent made a reversible local contract decision based on the existing one-shot barrier consumer: one global broadcast per instance, retained for late waiters; a new round uses a fresh AgentPager. This scope is now explicit in class/wait/broadcast docstrings. Executable AST is unchanged. An isolated fixture validates waiting, multicast wake-up, late/repeated retained reads, and independent fresh instances. C0279 is rejected under this documented current contract, not because repeated-message delivery was implemented or because the original behavior observation was false. If reusable successive delivery becomes a requirement, it needs a distinct design with per-generation consumption and this scenario applies again. The independent unicast wake-up defect C0278 remains OPEN and was re-reproduced.
